sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `codex-family`
- Canonical name: Codex family (`claim-codex-family-w2-identity`)
- Current status: active repository; stable 0.147.0 and prerelease 0.148.0-alpha.6 at capture (`claim-codex-family-w2-status`, `claim-codex-family-w2-release-status`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-10

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a product family with CLI, desktop, IDE, cloud, remote, API, integration, and scheduled routes (`claim-codex-family-w2-identity`, `claim-codex-family-w2-primary-type`, `claim-codex-family-w2-unique`).
- What it is not: one uniform surface (`claim-codex-family-w2-not-for`, `claim-codex-family-w2-drawback`). The ChatGPT mobile route is a client, not proof of a standalone Codex mobile app (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-remote`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-codex-family-w2-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: local Codex owns local threads and turns; managed Codex owns cloud tasks; desktop, IDE, and mobile may act as clients (`claim-codex-family-w2-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: same-device local execution, OpenAI-managed cloud containers, connected-computer relay, and SSH-host paths remain separate (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cli`, `claim-codex-family-w2-security-data`, `claim-codex-family-w2-execution-topology`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-codex-family-cli-local`, `surface-codex-family-cli-exec`, `surface-codex-family-desktop-local`, `surface-codex-family-ide-local`, `surface-codex-family-cloud-web`, `surface-codex-family-ios-remote`, `surface-codex-family-android-remote`, `surface-codex-family-desktop-ssh`, `surface-codex-family-app-server-local`, `surface-codex-family-cli-remote-tui`, `surface-codex-family-sdk`, `surface-codex-family-mcp-server`, `surface-codex-family-github-cloud`, `surface-codex-family-slack-cloud`, `surface-codex-family-linear-cloud`, `surface-codex-family-scheduled-local`, `surface-codex-family-scheduled-web`, `surface-codex-family-vendor-relay`, `surface-codex-family-generic-ssh`, `surface-codex-family-termux`.
- Execution location: same-device local, OpenAI-managed cloud, connected user computer, or user-controlled SSH host (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cli`, `claim-codex-family-w2-security-data`, `claim-codex-family-w2-execution-topology`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: local Codex supports OpenAI and configurable provider/model routes; cloud model availability and quotas are not fully public (`claim-codex-family-w2-provider-support`).
- Auth strategy: ChatGPT sign-in and API keys are local options; cloud features require ChatGPT authentication (`claim-codex-family-w2-auth`).
- Provider support: OpenAI, custom providers, Ollama, LM Studio, and Amazon Bedrock are documented (`claim-codex-family-w2-provider-support`). The Chat Completions versus Responses transport wording remains contradictory.

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: local thread history persists under `CODEX_HOME` when enabled (`claim-codex-family-w2-context-sessions`).
- Memory: `unknown` in the repaired candidate; no composite session claim is used as memory proof.
- Compaction: `unknown` in the repaired candidate; exact per-model limits remain provider-specific.
- Session behavior: persistence is configurable, while app-server threads support start, resume, fork, steering, streamed events, listing, and archival (`claim-codex-family-w2-context-sessions`, `claim-codex-family-w2-session-appserver`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: local tools, plugins, MCP, and app-server controls are surface-specific (`claim-codex-family-w2-extension-stack`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`).
- Extensions: skills, plugins, MCP, connectors, and hooks (`claim-codex-family-w2-extension-stack`).
- MCP: client support and a separate Codex MCP server are documented (`claim-codex-family-w2-extension-stack`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-mcp-server`).
- Skills: supported (`claim-codex-family-w2-extension-stack`).
- Hooks: supported (`claim-codex-family-w2-extension-stack`).
- APIs: app-server, TypeScript SDK, exec automation, and MCP server are separate API or surface claims (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-sdk`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cli`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-mcp-server`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: specialized subagents can receive follow-up input, run, and return combined results (`claim-codex-family-w2-orchestration`).
- Parallelism: subagent work can run concurrently; desktop worktrees isolate chat work, while no parallel-cloud claim is retained from the flagged source (`claim-codex-family-w2-orchestration`, `claim-codex-family-w2-worktrees`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: local OS sandbox and cloud isolated containers are distinct boundaries; desktop can also use managed Git worktrees (`claim-codex-family-w2-security-data`, `claim-codex-family-w2-worktrees`).
- Permissions: local approval policy and remote-client approvals vary by surface (`claim-codex-family-w2-security-data`).
- Security: public or untrusted exposure is warned against (`claim-codex-family-w2-not-for`); direct WebSocket app-server transport is experimental (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`).
- Data path: local host resources and selected auth policy differ from managed cloud task data and workspace policy (`claim-codex-family-w2-security-data`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local terminal/Desktop/IDE: `surface-codex-family-cli-local`, `surface-codex-family-cli-exec`, `surface-codex-family-desktop-local`, `surface-codex-family-ide-local` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cli`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-desktop`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-ide`).
  - Managed cloud: `surface-codex-family-cloud-web`, `surface-codex-family-github-cloud`, `surface-codex-family-slack-cloud`, `surface-codex-family-linear-cloud` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cloud`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-github`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-slack`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-linear`).
  - Native mobile clients and relay: `surface-codex-family-ios-remote`, `surface-codex-family-android-remote`, `surface-codex-family-vendor-relay` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-remote`).
  - SSH and app-server: `surface-codex-family-desktop-ssh`, `surface-codex-family-app-server-local`, `surface-codex-family-cli-remote-tui` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-remote`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`).
  - Programmatic: `surface-codex-family-sdk`, `surface-codex-family-mcp-server` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-sdk`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-mcp-server`).
  - Scheduled: `surface-codex-family-scheduled-local`, `surface-codex-family-scheduled-web` (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-scheduled`).
  - Generic or unverified: `surface-codex-family-generic-ssh`, `surface-codex-family-termux` (`claim-codex-family-w2-access-generic-ssh`, `claim-codex-family-w2-access-termux`).
- Remote behavior: mobile Remote uses a secure relay to a connected computer; desktop SSH starts a remote app-server; direct WebSocket is experimental (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-remote`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`).
- Mobile behavior: ChatGPT iOS and Android clients are verified; a standalone Codex mobile app, mobile-web parity, and Termux support remain unknown (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-remote`, `claim-codex-family-w2-access-termux`).
- Background behavior: cloud tasks, GitHub/Linear triggers, and local or web schedules have distinct hosts and continuity (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-cloud`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-github`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-linear`, `claim-codex-family-w2-surface-scheduled`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Free $0, Go $8, Plus $20, Pro from $100, Business $20 annual or $25 monthly per user, Enterprise/Edu contact sales (`claim-codex-family-w2-pricing`).
- License: CLI repository is Apache-2.0; CLI, SDK, and app-server are open source, while IDE and cloud are not (`claim-codex-family-w2-license-cli`, `claim-codex-family-w2-license-mixed`).
- Maintenance: active repository with stable and prerelease versions recorded separately (`claim-codex-family-w2-status`, `claim-codex-family-w2-release-status`).
- Lock-in: local open components and custom providers offer technical exit paths, while cloud and first-party clients depend on ChatGPT auth and workspace policy (`claim-codex-family-w2-license-mixed`, `claim-codex-family-w2-auth`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: Open Interpreter declares itself a fork of Codex (`claim-open-interpreter-lineage`).
- Relationship edges: no new outgoing Codex row. New inbound Wave 2 rows are `goose --connects_via--> codex-family`, `goose --reuses_auth_from--> codex-family`, and `goose --orchestrates--> codex-family`, supported in the Goose dossier. Existing baseline tuples were not copied.

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `unknown`; no new Wave 2 neighborhood row was emitted.
- Substitutes: `unknown`
- Partial substitutes: `unknown`
- Same-lineage relatives: `unknown`
- Often-confused products: `unknown`
- Complements: Goose has documented ACP and subagent compatibility, but no comparison membership was asserted.

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: open local runtime plus first-party cloud, desktop, IDE, mobile supervision, app-server, and SDK (`claim-codex-family-w2-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: surface variance, connected-host needs, and cloud setup (`claim-codex-family-w2-drawback`); API-key cloud limits (`claim-codex-family-w2-auth`); experimental WebSocket transport (`claim-codex-family-w2-surface-appserver`).
- Best fit: official positioning covers terminal and IDE developers, teams delegating cloud work, and managed workspaces (`claim-codex-family-w2-intended`). This is not a recommendation.
- Not-for: public untrusted execution and uniform-surface assumptions (`claim-codex-family-w2-not-for`).
